title: Associated-module chart and pointed basis presentation
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, $A$ a normed field and $L$ a lisse module for its all-continuous coefficient ring [def-sfb-norm-continuous-monodromy-data]. Let $H$ be a Hausdorff coefficient group with an open-subgroup basis, compact or two-sided complete, and $P$ a continuous right torsor [def-sfb-continuous-right-torsor]. Fix $n\geq0$ and a continuous homomorphism $r:H\to\operatorname{GL}_n(A)$. An associated-module presentation assigns to every section $s\in P(U)$ an actual slice frame $e_s:R_A^n|_U\simeq L|_U$ [def-sfb-associated-module-slice-frames], naturally under every restriction, satisfying $e_{sh}=e_s r(h)$ for every continuous local $h$. The entries of $r(h)$ are specified through the canonical continuous-ring comparison [def-sfb-continuous-ring-canonical-comparison]. An isomorphism respects two presentations when it carries all their frame columns to one another on every slice. If $X$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], fix a separable closure $k^s/k$ [def-pd-separable-closure], a field embedding $i:k^s\to K$, a point $x:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$, $p\in P_x$ and a family $b_j\in V_A(L)$ [def-sfb-normal-generic-lisse-sections]. Say the family is pointed at $p$ when a chart section $s$ admits a generic lift $t:\operatorname{Spec}k^s\to U$ such that its specialization along $i$ lies over $x$ and maps $s$ to $p$, and the actual generic restriction of every column of $e_s$ is $b_j$. This predicate does not itself assert that the family is a basis.
